00 — Learning Paths: Index

The one idea: the notes in this knowledge base already cover data engineering, Databricks, ML and AI applications from first principles to senior practice. What a beginner needs is the order: what to read, what to build, and how to know you are ready for the next level. These paths give that order, for four roles.

1. The four tracks

Track You end up able to Path
Data engineer Design, build, test and run reliable batch and streaming pipelines on open formats 01 Data Engineer Track
Databricks engineer Own a Databricks platform: Unity Catalog, Lakeflow, compute, cost, security, CI/CD, sharing 02 Databricks Engineer Track
ML engineer Take models from data to production: features, training, evaluation, serving, monitoring, LLMs 03 ML Engineer Track
AI engineer Build chatbots, MCP tools, agents and voice assistants that are grounded, safe and measured 05 AI Engineer Track
All tracks Prove it: certifications and a portfolio 04 Certifications and Portfolio

The tracks share their first level. Data engineering is the foundation of the other two.

2. The four levels

Level Name Can do Typical time
L1 Foundation Write SQL and Python for data, explain the lakehouse, run a notebook 4 to 6 weeks
L2 Practitioner Build a pipeline or model end to end with tests, on one platform 2 to 3 months
L3 Professional Design for reliability, cost and governance, debug performance, mentor others 6 to 12 months of practice
L4 Senior Make platform and architecture decisions, set standards, lead incidents and reviews Years of practice

Time assumes about 10 hours a week alongside a job. Levels are reached by building, not reading. Each level ends with a project and a checklist.

3. How these notes were checked for gaps (2026-10-26)

Every set was reviewed against what each role needs at each level.

Area Covered by Gap found, and filled by
SQL, Python, Git SQL, Python & DE, Git, Polars No gap
Data engineering concepts Data Engineering 01–11 No hands-on Databricks path for a beginner → 12 Hands-On from Zero. No PySpark API reference → 13 PySpark Cookbook
Lakehouse internals and Databricks services Open Lakehouse 01–19 No gap
A real end-to-end domain project Financial Data Engine 00–12 No gap
ML fundamentals AI & ML Foundations (overview only) No from-scratch training, evaluation, trees, deep learning → ML Engineering 01, 03, 06
Features and leakage Scattered → ML 02 Features and Feature Stores
Financial ML None → ML 04 Forecasting, ML 05 Credit Risk
LLMs LLM Engineering & RAG, AI stack Fine-tuning mechanics → ML 07 Fine-Tuning and LoRA
Building AI apps (chatbots, MCP, agents, voice, security, evals) LLM Engineering & RAG (overview only) No build guides → AI Engineering 01–09 and the AI Engineer Track
MLOps Partial (AI stack chapter) → ML 08 MLOps on Databricks
Testing, observability, security, cloud Testing, Observability, Security, CI/CD & Azure No gap
A beginner-to-senior order None → this set

4. How to use a track

  1. Start at the first level you can't yet tick off completely.
  2. Read the notes in the order listed, and do every exercise. They take under two hours each.
  3. Build the level's project. Put it in Git with a README.
  4. Tick the checklist honestly. If an item fails, reread that note and redo its exercise.
  5. Move on only when every item passes.
